newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bad loan problem still substantial - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan bad loan problem still substantial - BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told business executives on Monday that Japan's financial institutions are tackling their bad loans, but the problem remains substantial.
"The financial firms are working to resolve the problem, but the size of the bad loans to be dealt with is still substantial," he said.
Matsushita spoke on the first day of a two-day trip to western Japan.
He stressed that tackling bad loans was one of the most important issues for financial institutions to address and resolve.
He also said that banks should make further efforts to continue restructuring, disclosure of their business activities, and boosting their self-capitalisation.
He said that interim results released by banks recently showed that they were taking a positive attitude towards disposing of bad loans.

Matsushita said that there were two forces influencing the economy -- firstly, a favourable economic cycle which would move the economy upwards, and secondly, pressure from structural adjustment which was holding back the recovery.
However, long-term business restructuring had helped improve profits and changes in industrial structure were creating a new business environment.
"Pressures from structural adjustment will continue somewhat but the effect will gradually decrease," he said.
Matsushita also told business executives that currency rates should reflect each country's economic fundamentals.
"The industrialised countries of the world all agree on this point," he said.
He added that Japan would continue to exchange views with other industrialised nations and act to ensure the market would stabilise in a way that would reflect each country's fundamentals.
